status: research-informed draft; not applied to restaurant codes or regressions
normalization: Unicode NFKD, casefold, collapse punctuation/hyphens/apostrophes to spaces; preserve originals for adjudication. Latin-script variants first pass; native-script lexicon requires separate validation.

classification.candidate: Any dictionary hit creates an evidence candidate, not automatic confirmation.
classification.probable: One pre-election review mentioning a country-associated dish offered by the restaurant suffices for a cuisine flag.
classification.shared: One mention of a shared dish supports every cuisine linked to that dish. Match the longest named preparation at each position.
classification.negative: Exclude negated availability, wishes, another restaurant, reviewer background, comparisons and hypothetical dishes. Negative evaluations of a dish actually served still count as food evidence.
classification.multiple: Preserve multiple country associations rather than forcing one; avoid duplicating restaurants in pooled models.
classification.symmetry: Apply identical dictionary and evidence rules to ME and Mediterranean listings; keep label and cuisine evidence separate.
classification.pool: Start with all primary ME-family and Mediterranean listings, including keyword-negative restaurants; later audit generic labels separately.
classification.outcomes: Dictionary and coding use pre-election text only; no tuning on effects or p values.

cross_border_notes: Specificity is relative to these seven lists. Compare complete dish names, including aliases, and retain distinct named preparations.
Check ambiguous words in context before counting them as food mentions.
